label: prop:electron-period-base
title: CAL-1 ($m_e$) is the $n=0$ base period of the prolongation tower
html:
The prolonged Seiberg--Witten periods satisfy the one-parameter recurrence a_D^{(n+2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(n+1)} - a_D^{(n)} (Symplectic prolongation (det B = 1) gives a one-parameter recurrence). The n=0 term is the unprolonged period, the electron period a_D^{(e)} (The Seiberg–Witten differential is the jet decomposition of the Archimedean realisation). Identifying a_D^{(e)} with the leptonic scale m_e (CAL-1) establishes the first calibration as the base of the tower. Every period is generated from the triple (m_e,\,a_D^{(1)},\,\tau), and m_e propagates into every term through the recurrence rather than entering as an external multiplicative prefactor. Concretely, the n=2 period is a_D^{(2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(1)} - m_e.

That identity is derived from the recurrence together with the base condition a_0 = m_e. The base condition itself is part of the definition of the tower, not a result: it is the CAL-1 identification.
